   "id": "a025ef47",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# U.S. Weather Analysis 2014–2015 — Advanced EDA\n",
    "### Data Cleaning, Feature Engineering & Statistical Analysis across 10 U.S. Cities\n",
    "\n",
    "**Data source:** [FiveThirtyEight — U.S. Weather History](https://github.com/fivethirtyeight/data/tree/master/us-weather-history) (real Weather Underground station data, used in their published story)\n",
    "\n",
    "This notebook analyzes one year of daily weather records (mean/min/max temperature, historical averages, all-time records, and precipitation) across 10 major U.S. cities to answer real analytical questions:\n",
    "- Which cities are experiencing the most anomalous (record-breaking) weather?\n",
    "- How does temperature variability differ by city/climate zone?\n",
    "- Is there a statistically significant difference in temperature between cities?\n",
    "- What's the relationship between precipitation and temperature deviation?\n",
    "\n",
    "**Tools:** pandas, numpy, matplotlib, seaborn, scipy (statistical testing)\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "2ffae31a",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-08-17T04:46:36.122523Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-08-17T04:46:36.122319Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-08-17T04:46:38.058406Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-08-17T04:46:38.056680Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "import seaborn as sns\n",
    "from scipy import stats\n",
    "\n",
    "sns.set_theme(style=\"whitegrid\", palette=\"deep\")\n",
    "plt.rcParams['figure.dpi'] = 100\n",
    "pd.set_option('display.max_columns', 20)\n"
   ]
  },
  {

   "id": "51160bfa",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [

   ],
   "source": [
    "station_to_city = {\n",
    "    'KCLT': 'Charlotte',\n",
    "    'KCQT': 'Los Angeles',\n",
    "    'KHOU': 'Houston',\n",
    "    'KIND': 'Indianapolis',\n",
    "    'KJAX': 'Jacksonville',\n",
    "    'KMDW': 'Chicago',\n",
    "    'KNYC': 'New York',\n",
    "    'KPHL': 'Philadelphia',\n",
    "    'KPHX': 'Phoenix',\n",
    "    'KSEA': 'Seattle',\n",
    "}\n",
    "\n",
    "frames = []\n",
    "for station, city in station_to_city.items():\n",
    "    df_city = pd.read_csv(f'{station}.csv')\n",
    "    df_city['City'] = city\n",
    "    df_city['Station'] = station\n",
    "    frames.append(df_city)\n",
    "\n",
    "df = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)\n",
    "print(f\"Combined shape: {df.shape}\")\n",
    "df.head()\n"
   ]

   "source": [
    "## 3. Feature Engineering\n",
    "We derive analytical features not present in the raw data:\n",
    "- `Year`, `Month`, `MonthName` — for time-based grouping\n",
    "- `TempAnomaly` — how far actual mean temp deviates from the 134-year historical average\n",
    "- `NearRecordHigh` / `NearRecordLow` — flags for days within 3°F of an all-time record\n",
    "- `PrecipAnomaly` — actual precipitation minus historical average"
   ]
  },

   ],
   "source": [
    "df['Year'] = df['date'].dt.year\n",
    "df['Month'] = df['date'].dt.month\n",
    "df['MonthName'] = df['date'].dt.strftime('%b')\n",
    "\n",
    "df['HistoricalAvgTemp'] = (df['average_min_temp'] + df['average_max_temp']) / 2\n",
    "df['TempAnomaly'] = df['actual_mean_temp'] - df['HistoricalAvgTemp']\n",
    "\n",
    "df['NearRecordHigh'] = (df['record_max_temp'] - df['actual_max_temp']) <= 3\n",
    "df['NearRecordLow']  = (df['actual_min_temp'] - df['record_min_temp']) <= 3\n",
    "\n",
    "df['PrecipAnomaly'] = df['actual_precipitation'] - df['average_precipitation']\n",
    "\n",
    "df[['date','City','actual_mean_temp','HistoricalAvgTemp','TempAnomaly','NearRecordHigh','NearRecordLow']].head()\n"
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "city_stats = df.groupby('City').agg(\n",
    "    AvgMeanTemp=('actual_mean_temp', 'mean'),\n",
    "    TempStdDev=('actual_mean_temp', 'std'),\n",
    "    MaxTempRecorded=('actual_max_temp', 'max'),\n",
    "    MinTempRecorded=('actual_min_temp', 'min'),\n",
    "    TotalPrecipitation=('actual_precipitation', 'sum'),\n",
    "    DaysNearRecordHigh=('NearRecordHigh', 'sum'),\n",
    "    DaysNearRecordLow=('NearRecordLow', 'sum'),\n",
    ").round(2).sort_values('AvgMeanTemp', ascending=False)\n",
    "\n",
    "city_stats\n"
   ]

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "0fdff1e5",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 5. Monthly Temperature Trend — All Cities\n",
    "How does average temperature move across the year for each city, and how does it compare to the long-term historical average?"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 7,
   "id": "425ebcf1",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-08-17T04:46:38.202524Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-08-17T04:46:38.201933Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-08-17T04:46:38.763401Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-08-17T04:46:38.762457Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 1200x600 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "monthly = df.groupby(['City','Month'])['actual_mean_temp'].mean().reset_index()\n",
    "monthly_pivot = monthly.pivot(index='Month', columns='City', values='actual_mean_temp')\n",
    "\n",
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12,6))\n",
    "monthly_pivot.plot(ax=ax, marker='o', linewidth=2)\n",
    "ax.set_title('Average Monthly Temperature by City (2014-2015)', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')\n",
    "ax.set_xlabel('Month')\n",
    "ax.set_ylabel('Avg Temperature (°F)')\n",
    "ax.set_xticks(range(1,13))\n",
    "ax.legend(bbox_to_anchor=(1.02,1), loc='upper left', title='City')\n",
    "plt.tight_layout()\n",
    "plt.savefig('chart1_monthly_trend.png', dpi=120, bbox_inches='tight')\n",
    "plt.show()\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "77a00f31",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 6. Temperature Anomaly Heatmap\n",
    "Which city-month combinations deviated most from their 134-year historical average? Red = warmer than usual, blue = colder than usual."

  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",

   "source": [
    "anomaly_pivot = df.groupby(['City','Month'])['TempAnomaly'].mean().reset_index().pivot(index='City', columns='Month', values='TempAnomaly')\n",
    "\n",
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12,6))\n",
    "sns.heatmap(anomaly_pivot, cmap='RdBu_r', center=0, annot=True, fmt='.1f',\n",
    "            cbar_kws={'label': 'Temp Anomaly (°F vs historical avg)'}, ax=ax)\n",
    "ax.set_title('Monthly Temperature Anomaly by City', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')\n",
    "ax.set_xlabel('Month')\n",
    "ax.set_ylabel('City')\n",
    "plt.tight_layout()\n",
    "plt.savefig('chart2_anomaly_heatmap.png', dpi=120, bbox_inches='tight')\n",
    "plt.show()\n"
   ]
  },

   ]

   ],
   "source": [
    "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14,5))\n",
    "\n",
    "total_precip = df.groupby('City')['actual_precipitation'].sum().sort_values(ascending=False)\n",
    "total_precip.plot(kind='bar', ax=axes[0], color=sns.color_palette('deep', len(total_precip)))\n",
    "axes[0].set_title('Total Annual Precipitation by City', fontweight='bold')\n",
    "axes[0].set_ylabel('Total Precipitation (inches)')\n",
    "axes[0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)\n",
    "\n",
    "rainy_days = df[df['actual_precipitation'] > 0.1].groupby('City').size().sort_values(ascending=False)\n",
    "rainy_days.plot(kind='bar', ax=axes[1], color=sns.color_palette('deep', len(rainy_days)))\n",
    "axes[1].set_title('Number of Rainy Days (>0.1 in) by City', fontweight='bold')\n",
    "axes[1].set_ylabel('Days')\n",
    "axes[1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)\n",
    "\n",
    "plt.tight_layout()\n",
    "plt.savefig('chart3_precipitation.png', dpi=120, bbox_inches='tight')\n",
    "plt.show()\n"
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "## 9. Correlation Analysis\n",
    "How do the numeric weather variables relate to each other?"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 11,
   "id": "8adad006",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {

   ],
   "source": [
    "num_cols = ['actual_mean_temp','actual_min_temp','actual_max_temp','actual_precipitation','TempAnomaly','PrecipAnomaly']\n",
    "corr = df[num_cols].corr()\n",
    "\n",
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8,6))\n",
    "sns.heatmap(corr, annot=True, fmt='.2f', cmap='coolwarm', center=0, square=True, ax=ax)\n",
    "ax.set_title('Correlation Matrix — Weather Variables', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')\n",
    "plt.tight_layout()\n",
    "plt.savefig('chart5_correlation.png', dpi=120, bbox_inches='tight')\n",
    "plt.show()\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "08f8cce0",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "**Finding:** As expected, `actual_min_temp` and `actual_max_temp` are highly correlated with `actual_mean_temp` (they compose it). More interesting: `TempAnomaly` and `PrecipAnomaly` show a weak-to-moderate relationship — investigated further in Section 12."
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "## 11. Statistical Test — Is the Temperature Difference Between Cities Significant?\n",
    "We use a one-way ANOVA test to check whether the difference in mean temperature across cities is statistically significant (not just due to random chance).\n",
    "\n",
    "**Hypotheses:**\n",
    "- H0 (null): All cities have the same mean temperature\n",
    "- H1 (alternative): At least one city's mean temperature differs significantly"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 13,
   "id": "b675ece7",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-08-17T04:46:41.006323Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-08-17T04:46:41.005519Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-08-17T04:46:41.024494Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-08-17T04:46:41.023622Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "F-statistic: 120.78\n",
      "P-value: 3.72e-199\n",
      "\n",
      "Result: Statistically significant difference in temperature across cities (p < 0.05).\n",
      "This confirms city/climate zone is a meaningful driver of temperature variation in this dataset.\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "groups = [df[df['City']==c]['actual_mean_temp'].values for c in df['City'].unique()]\n",
    "f_stat, p_value = stats.f_oneway(*groups)\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"F-statistic: {f_stat:.2f}\")\n",
    "print(f\"P-value: {p_value:.2e}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "if p_value < 0.05:\n",
    "    print(\"\\nResult: Statistically significant difference in temperature across cities (p < 0.05).\")\n",
    "    print(\"This confirms city/climate zone is a meaningful driver of temperature variation in this dataset.\")\n",
    "else:\n",
    "    print(\"\\nResult: No statistically significant difference found.\")\n"
   ]
  },

   ]

   "source": [
    "## 13. Trend Smoothing — 7-Day Rolling Average (New York example)\n",
    "Daily temperature is noisy. A 7-day rolling average reveals the underlying seasonal trend more clearly, and highlights how far actual temps ran from the historical average across the year."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 15,
   "id": "ffcd0472",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-08-17T04:46:41.569311Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-08-17T04:46:41.569143Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-08-17T04:46:42.046517Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-08-17T04:46:42.045408Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 1300x500 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "ny = df[df['City']=='New York'].sort_values('date').copy()\n",
    "ny['RollingAvgTemp'] = ny['actual_mean_temp'].rolling(7, center=True).mean()\n",
    "ny['RollingHistAvg'] = ny['HistoricalAvgTemp'].rolling(7, center=True).mean()\n",
    "\n",
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(13,5))\n",
    "ax.plot(ny['date'], ny['actual_mean_temp'], alpha=0.25, color='gray', label='Daily actual (raw)')\n",
    "ax.plot(ny['date'], ny['RollingAvgTemp'], color='crimson', linewidth=2, label='7-day rolling avg (actual)')\n",
    "ax.plot(ny['date'], ny['RollingHistAvg'], color='steelblue', linewidth=2, linestyle='--', label='Historical average')\n",
    "ax.set_title('New York: Actual vs Historical Temperature Trend (7-day smoothed)', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')\n",
    "ax.set_ylabel('Temperature (°F)')\n",
    "ax.legend()\n",
    "plt.tight_layout()\n",
    "plt.savefig('chart7_rolling_avg_nyc.png', dpi=120, bbox_inches='tight')\n",
    "plt.show()\n"
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "## 14. Key Findings & Summary\n",
    "\n",
    "1. **No data quality issues at source** — but feature engineering (anomaly calculations, record-proximity flags) was required to make the data analytically useful.\n",
    "2. **Statistically significant temperature differences exist between cities** (ANOVA p-value ≪ 0.05) — confirming climate zone is a real driver, not noise.\n",
    "3. **Seattle and Los Angeles ran the warmest relative to their own historical averages** (+3.9°F and +3.1°F respectively) over the study period, while **Indianapolis ran coldest relative to its average** (-1.8°F) — notably, this is about relative anomaly, not absolute temperature (Phoenix is still the hottest city in absolute terms).\n",
    "4. **Temperature anomaly and precipitation anomaly show a weak correlation** — warmer-than-usual days are not strongly linked to wetter or drier conditions in this dataset.\n",
    "5. **Extreme event detection** flags the specific days each city came within 3°F of an all-time record — useful for climate-risk style reporting.\n",
    "\n",
    "## Files Produced\n",
    "- `combined_weather_data.csv` — cleaned, combined, feature-engineered dataset (3,650 rows)\n",
    "- 7 chart PNGs (`chart1`–`chart7`)\n",
